title: A final indexing object computes a coherent colimit
statement: An infinity category means a simplicial set with fillers for every inner horn, where an inner horn is the union of the faces of the standard simplex except one face other than the first or last. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the nerve of $\{0<\cdots<n\}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Colimits are understood in the coherent mapping-space sense: a cocone with vertex $L$ is a colimit when, for every object $T$, composition induces an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}(L,T)$ to the space of coherent cocones with vertex $T$. Let $J$ and $\mathcal C$ be infinity categories, let $t$ be a final object of $J$, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is contractible for every object $j$ of $J$, and let $p:J\to\mathcal C$ be a functor. Then $p$ has a colimit with vertex $p(t)$. One can choose its cocone so that its edge at $t$ is the identity of $p(t)$. In particular, for every $n\geq0$ and every diagram $p:\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$, its value $p(n)$ at the last vertex is a colimit, with the cocone induced by the order-preserving map $[n+1]\to[n]$ which fixes $0,\ldots,n$ and sends $n+1$ to $n$.

source.place: Kerodon Example 7.2.1.4 (03LQ), together with the colimit dual of Corollary 7.2.2.11 (02XU), https://kerodon.net/tag/02XU, and Corollary 7.2.3.6 (02XY), https://kerodon.net/tag/02XY. Also used in HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4. Online text read; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag gives coherent cofinality.

proof.text: Let $i:\{t\}\hookrightarrow J$ be the vertex inclusion. The hypothesis on $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is exactly the final-object hypothesis in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne]. Its equivalence therefore makes $i$ right anodyne. This uses contractibility of the full mapping spaces, not just uniqueness of arrows in the homotopy category.

Apply the pushout-join clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to $i$ and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. Since joining with the empty set leaves a simplicial set unchanged, it makes $J\amalg_{\{t\}}\{t\}^{\triangleright}\hookrightarrow J^{\triangleright}$ inner anodyne. Map this domain to $\mathcal C$ by $p$ on $J$ and by the degenerate edge $\operatorname{id}_{p(t)}$ on $\{t\}^{\triangleright}=\Delta^1$. These maps agree at $t$. The inner-horn filler property of $\mathcal C$ gives extension across any inner anodyne map: lift successively across its horn attachments, take the compatible union at a limit ordinal, and pass to a retract. Thus there is $\bar p:J^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ extending these data, with apex exactly $p(t)$ and component at $t$ exactly its identity. It yields a coherent transformation $\alpha:p\to\Delta_Jp(t)$: precompose with the simplicial map $J\times\Delta^1\to J^{\triangleright}$ which on a simplex retains the initial $J$-vertices labelled $0$ and sends every vertex labelled $1$ to the new cone point. This ordered rule commutes with faces and degeneracies and retains the prescribed identity edge. Here the internal functor simplicial set and its edges have exactly the transformation meaning specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4 and Example 4.3.6.5; agent expansion of the lifting and explicit cone-to-transformation map.

proof.text: For any $T\in\mathcal C$, put $\operatorname{Coc}_J(p,T)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)}(p,\Delta_JT)$, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. By the mapping-space clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], restriction $r_T:\operatorname{Coc}_J(p,T)\to\operatorname{Coc}_{\{t\}}(p(t),T)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(t),T)$ is an equivalence. Postcomposition of $\alpha$ gives $c_T:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(t),T)\to\operatorname{Coc}_J(p,T)$. Compatibility of restriction with composition gives $r_Tc_T(u)=u\circ\alpha_t\simeq u$ on the entire mapping space, since $\alpha_t=\operatorname{id}_{p(t)}$. Hence $r_Tc_T$ is homotopic to the identity and $r_T$ is an equivalence, so $c_T$ is an equivalence. This is precisely the stated coherent universal property of a colimit with vertex $p(t)$. This argument proves the same assertion for every cocone whose component at $t$ is the identity, not only for the extension chosen in Step 2.

source.place: Opposite-category dual of Proposition 7.2.2.1, conditions (1) and (6), via right cofinality of right anodyne monomorphisms. Agent-written mapping-space two-out-of-three argument.

proof.text: For $J=\Delta^n=N([n])$, compatible inner-horn data extend to an ordered chain: in dimension $2$ this is transitivity of the two consecutive inequalities, and in dimensions at least $3$ the horn fixes all edges, with all remaining inequalities following from their order. A simplex of the nerve is exactly its ordered chain, so this supplies the required inner fillers. Its right-pinched mapping space from $j$ to $n$ has exactly one simplex in every degree: it is the ordered chain with all initial vertices equal to $j$ and last vertex $n$. All its simplicial operators are therefore those of a point. Thus $n$ is final, including $n=0$. These are direct checks from the simplex description and the mapping-space definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], over the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: Definition 4.7.3.1 and Example 4.7.3.5; elementary ordered-chain calculation for the standard simplex.

proof.text: Identify $(\Delta^n)^{\triangleright}$ with $\Delta^{n+1}$. The order map $r:[n+1]\to[n]$, $r(k)=k$ for $k\leq n$ and $r(n+1)=n$, gives the cocone $p\circ N(r)$ with apex $p(n)$. On the edge $\{n,n+1\}$ it is the degeneracy at $p(n)$, hence the identity. Step 4 verifies the final-object hypothesis, so Step 1 makes $\{n\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ right anodyne, and the mapping-space calculation of Step 3 applies to this particular cocone as well. Consequently the displayed explicit cocone is colimiting; when $n=0$ it is just the identity edge, so the boundary case is included.

source.place: The mapping-space restriction criterion of Proposition 7.2.2.1, dualized, applied to the explicit standard-simplex cocone; compare Corollary 7.2.2.6 (02XW).
